title: Chimps Can Be Thieves, But They Hesitate to Rob Their Friends - Nautilus
author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyChimps Can Be Thieves, But They Hesitate to Rob Their FriendsAnd their friends were quicker to forgive them for their thieveryDRBy Devin Reese9:00 AM CST on November 5, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHumans obviously behave differently toward their friends than they do strangers. Case in point: We’re much more likely to loan money to a friend than a stranger. It appears that our closest relatives also differentiate between friends and strangers—especially when it comes to deciding who to steal treats from according to a recent study published in the journal Evolution and Human Behavior.Experimental psychologists watched 26 adult chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes) during 30-minute feeding times at the Ngamba Island Chimpanzee Sanctuary in Uganda to ascertain which ones were closely bonded via grooming each other, eating together, or otherwise making body contact or hanging out near each other. Next, chimps selected as study subjects were paired with either their closest “friend” or a not-very-close chimp. One chimp (the “victim”) was put in a room with access to three trays baited with large chunks of pineapple. Another chimp (the “thief”) watched the trays being loaded up, and, after the victim enjoyed one of the pineapple chunks, it was given the opportunity to steal the other pieces of fruit.Read more: “What Became of the Chimps Who Revolutionized Our Understanding of Animal Behavior?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
